reason: Identical wording; only capitalisation of Churches differs.
Same seven-fold doxology with Amen at both ends; Latin lacks articles and verb, English wording only.
Reins means kidneys; children killed with death, searcher of hearts, recompense by works all agree.
Stars fall like unripe figs shaken by a strong wind; mighty versus great is English wording.
Carried away in the spirit to a wilderness; scarlet beast, blasphemous names, seven heads, ten horns agree.
Same address to Ephesus, holder of seven stars walking among seven golden lampstands.
Latin tamen and Greek only both introduce the command to hold fast until I come.
Commanded or told not to harm vegetation, only unsealed people; wording only.
A third of living sea creatures die and a third of ships are destroyed in both.
Mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; power to continue versus authority to act forty-two months is wording.
Identical refrain to the churches.
Fourth trumpet strikes a third of sun, moon and stars; day and night darkened by a third.
The woman is the great city reigning over the kings of the earth in both.
Latin present miraris versus Greek past did you marvel; otherwise the same mystery of woman and beast.
Latin Factum est is singular 'It is done' where the Greek is plural 'They have come to be'; rest agrees.
Took the little scroll, ate it, sweet as honey in the mouth, belly bitter; wording only.
Another angel with a sharp sickle comes from the heavenly temple in both.
Bottomless pit renders the shaft of the abyss; smoke like a furnace darkens sun and air.
KJV adds 'Amen' (Textus Receptus) and orders 'hell and death' against Greek 'death and Hades'.
Latin adds 'et qui venturus es' (who are to come), absent from the Greek title.
Latin afflicts with heat ('aestu') and fire where Greek scorches with fire; Latin names the angel.
Another angel descending with great authority; earth lit by his glory in both.
KJV has 'O Lord' and 'shalt be' where the Greek has 'the Holy One'; the title differs by textual reading.
Second bowl turns sea to blood like a dead man's; every living soul in the sea dies.
Latin adds 'eorum Deus' (their God), absent from the Greek; Latin singular populus versus Greek peoples.
Lamb shepherds and leads to living waters; God wipes every tear; living fountains versus springs of life is wording.
KJV (TR) has an extra 'hast laboured' and different clause order; Greek has endurance, bore up, not grown weary.
Army singular versus armies plural; two hundred thousand thousand equals two myriads of myriads.
Reed like a rod given; told to rise and measure temple, altar and worshippers.
Blessed reader and hearers who keep the prophecy; time near; 'this prophecy' is wording.
Twenty-four elders seated on thrones before God fall on their faces and worship.
Seated one like jasper and sardius; rainbow like emerald around the throne.
KJV adds 'I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last' and 'which are in Asia', absent from the Greek.
Locusts forbidden to harm grass, green things, trees; only men without God's seal; signum renders seal.
Latin future, those adulterers 'will be' in tribulation, and repent of 'their' works; Greek: I throw them, repent of her works.
Second woe past; third woe coming quickly in both.
Latin hears the voice of one eagle and the angels about to sound the trumpet; Greek hears the eagle; minor arrangement.
Latin adds 'enim ... ante thronum Dei' (before God's throne); Greek ends simply 'they are unblemished'.
Rest killed by the rider's mouth-sword; birds filled with their flesh.
God puts it in their hearts to do his will, agree, and give the kingdom to the beast.
Smoke of torment rises forever; no rest day or night for beast-worshippers and mark-bearers.
Star named Wormwood; third of waters bitter; many die from the waters.
Latin says the Lamb 'opened' (aperuisset) the book; the Greek says he took the scroll.
Salvation, power, kingdom and Christ's authority come; accuser of the brothers cast down; wording only.
Heaven opened, white horse, rider Faithful and True judges and wars in righteousness.
Latin stetit, like the Greek, has the dragon standing on the sand; it versus he is English.
KJV (TR) adds 'great' ('that great city, the holy Jerusalem') where Greek has 'the holy city Jerusalem'.
Latin gives authority over 'four parts' of the earth, Greek a fourth; Latin 'to him' versus 'to them', lacks 'I saw'.
Sixth seal: great earthquake, sun black as haircloth sackcloth, whole moon like blood.
Mighty angel throws a millstone into the sea; Babylon thrown down and never found again.
Great dragon, ancient serpent, Devil and Satan, world-deceiver thrown to earth with his angels.
Wall built of jasper; city pure gold like clear glass in both.
KJV (TR) has repent of 'their deeds' where the Greek has 'her works'; future 'will cast' versus present.
They say to mountains and rocks: fall on us, hide us from the throne-sitter and the Lamb's wrath.
KJV (TR) adds 'I saw' at the opening, absent from the Greek; the wounded head and marvelling world agree.
KJV adds the object 'thee' after fear; judgments versus righteous acts is wording; otherwise parallel.
Latin 'tertius angelus' lacks Greek 'another', which reads 'another angel, a third'; warning otherwise identical.
Latin future singular 'congregabit' (he will gather) versus Greek past plural 'they gathered'; Armagedon spelling.
Dragon thrown into the abyss, shut and sealed, until the thousand years end; then briefly released.
Latin adds 'principium et finis' (the beginning and the end), absent from the Greek here.
Clothed in a blood-dipped garment, named the Word of God; past versus present is English.
Horses and riders with fiery, hyacinth and sulfur breastplates; lion heads; fire, smoke, sulfur from mouths.
Great dragon, ancient serpent, devil and Satan, deceiver of the world, cast down with his angels.
Latin repeats 'signati' (sealed) after each tribe; the Greek verse lists the counts without it.
Little scroll open in hand; right foot on sea, left on earth.
Neither cold nor hot; would that you were cold or hot.
KJV (TR) repeats 'were sealed' for Reuben and Gad; Greek has 'sealed' only with Judah; Juda spelling is wording.
Latin repeats 'signati' for Reuben and Gad; Greek gives 'sealed' only with Judah.
KJV (TR) has horns 'upon the beast'; the Greek has horns 'and the beast', making the beast a co-agent.
Latin adds 'in sanguine Agni' (in the blood of the Lamb), absent from the Greek.
KJV 'have drunk of the wine' versus Greek 'have fallen from the wine'; a different verb by textual reading.
Latin seven burning lamps lack Greek 'of fire'; lightnings, voices, thunders and seven spirits agree.
Latin 'dicere' (to say/sing) the song versus Greek 'learn' the song; otherwise parallel.
New song before throne, living creatures, elders; only the 144,000 purchased from the earth could learn it.
Dragon, thrown to earth, pursues the woman who bore the male child.
KJV (TR) orders 'saw ... and heard' while the Greek has 'hearing and seeing'; otherwise parallel.
Opened the shaft of the abyss; furnace-like smoke darkens sun and air.
KJV presents falling, worshipping, casting crowns in present tense; the Greek uses future tense.
KJV (TR) repeats 'were sealed' after each tribe; Greek lists counts only; name spellings are wording.
Lamb on Mount Zion with 144,000 bearing his and his Father's name on foreheads.
Why marvel; mystery of woman and the beast with seven heads and ten horns.
Twelve gates of twelve pearls, each from one pearl; street pure gold like transparent glass.
I come quickly; blessed who keeps the prophecy of this book; Greek's opening 'And' is negligible.
KJV 'It is done' is singular where the Greek has plural 'They have come to be'; rest agrees.
Latin adds 'et vide' (and see) to the summons; the Greek has only 'Come'.
Same vice list and lake of fire and sulfur, the second death; accursed versus abominable is close.
Seven angels with seven plagues, clothed in pure bright linen, golden girdles on breasts.
KJV (TR) 'a few things against thee' versus Greek 'this against you'; Jezebel's teaching and seduction otherwise agree.
Beast, kings and armies gathered to wage war against the rider and his army.
KJV (TR) 'holy apostles' merges two groups; the Greek addresses saints and apostles separately; avenging agrees.
Latin 'et eos' makes heaven-dwellers a third object; Greek sets them in apposition to his tent.
Seventh sign: great red dragon, seven heads, ten horns, seven diadems.
Latin card includes 'Vobis autem dico' from Greek 2:24 (verse division); Latin 'opera sua' (their works) versus 'your works'.
KJV (TR): the captor goes captive and the killer must be killed; Greek: the one destined for captivity or sword meets it.
Four angels at four corners hold back the winds from earth, sea and trees.
Latin 'divinitatem' (divinity) stands where the Greek has 'wealth'; other six attributes agree.
Identical refrain; archaic phrasing only.
Hair like women's hair; teeth like lions' teeth.
Dragon, cast down to earth, pursues the woman who bore the male child.
Revelation given by God to show his servants what must soon happen, signified through his angel to John.
